flagged.evidence: The Statement defines the componentwise integral using g_1 through g_m, and Proof 2.1 chooses i in {1,...,m} and puts u:=g_i. The cited items/lem-standard-basis-of-f-n.md states: "Every index runs from $0$, so the coordinates of an element of $F^{n}$ are $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$"; items/def-euclidean-inner-product.md defines R^m as functions m→R and x_k:=x(k) for k<m. Thus g_m is undefined under the supplied coordinate convention; for m=1 the displayed integral uses undefined g_1 and omits the sole coordinate g_0. No local reindexing g_i(x):=g(x)(i-1) is defined. The componentwise integral definition and component selection therefore require corrected indices or an explicit reindexing.
